item.text:
“Runs locally” doesn’t necessarily mean “runs on your laptop.”

Mistral Large 4’s release is a useful reminder of that distinction.

According to Hugging Face’s introduction, its 2-bit quantized versions can run on a single Apple Silicon Ultra machine—with 512 GB of unified memory. Other configurations require distributed inference or multiple GPUs.

That’s meaningful flexibility. But it’s also substantial infrastructure.

For teams evaluating open-weight models, I’d separate three questions:

→ Can we run it?
→ Can we run it at acceptable quality and speed?
→ Can we operate it reliably at a sustainable cost?

Quantization can reduce memory requirements, but teams still need to measure quality on their own tasks. Context length, concurrency, and hardware choices also shape the deployment experience.

The exciting part isn’t that every organization should self-host a trillion-parameter model.

It’s that organizations have more deployment options—and can evaluate which trade-offs make sense for their workloads.

When would you choose self-hosting over a managed endpoint?

#EnterpriseAI #LLM #AIInfrastructure #Mistral
